title: Monas Hieroglyphica (Latin, 1591)
author: John Dee
description: Monas Hieroglyphica (The Hieroglyphic Monad) by John Dee (1527-1608/9), the Elizabethan mathematician, astrologer and magus, here in a Latin edition dated 1591 (the work was first printed at Antwerp in 1564 and dedicated to the Emperor Maximilian II). In twenty-four theorems Dee presents a single composite glyph, the Monad, combining the symbols of the Moon, Sun, the cross of the elements and the sign of Aries, and expounds it geometrically, arithmetically, astronomically, alchemically and Kabbalistically as a universal key unifying all knowledge and expressing the structure of creation. Dee claimed the Monad would revolutionise astronomy, alchemy, mathematics, languages and mechanics. Notoriously cryptic, it influenced the Rosicrucian manifestos (the Monad appears in the Chymical Wedding of Christian Rosenkreutz) and remains a central text of Renaissance Hermetic and alchemical symbolism.
